(Internal) Classify and Pivot Long/Wide AST Data for the profile_* Family

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
dot-profile_tested_long_wide.Rd

Shared by every profile_* function that needs a group x event x class S/R/I matrix: profile_audit_support, profile_audit_interaction_support, and profile_prepare_model_data all call this once instead of each re-implementing the same long-to-wide classify-and-pivot. Not exported – this is specifically the classification step (mapping raw values to canonical R/S/I via resistant_values/etc.), which is resistance-profile-domain logic, not a generic preprocessing pivot; it is deliberately NOT the same job as anumaan's prep_create_wide_ast_matrix(), which pivots raw values verbatim with no classification and is for preprocessing-stage use.

Usage

.profile_tested_long_wide(
  data,
  group_col,
  class_cols,
  class_col,
  value_col,
  resistant_values,
  susceptible_values,
  intermediate_values,
  event_id_col,
  untested_values = c("NT", "Not tested", "not tested", "NA", "N/A"),
  unknown_action = c("error", "treat_as_untested"),
  conflict_action = c("error", "drop_conflicts", "resistant_wins", "susceptible_wins",
    "first"),
  intermediate_as_resistant = NULL
)

Details

One AST policy, applied identically everywhere this helper is used. Raw value parsing tries the caller's declared resistant_values/ susceptible_values/intermediate_values vocabulary first (exact match, case-insensitive), then falls back to prep_clean_ast_values's messy-string extraction (handles "S (HIGH LEVEL)", keyword scans, etc.) for anything that didn't match – the same parsing logic used everywhere else in anumaan, not a separate, cruder exact-match-only implementation kept just here. blank/NA/declared untested_values tokens are UNTESTED, not an outcome; a non-blank value that matches none of the above (declared vocabulary OR prep_clean_ast_values's extraction) is UNKNOWN, handled per unknown_action ("error", the default – a typo or an unanticipated lab code should be loud, not silently swept into "untested"; "treat_as_untested" to opt out when that is a deliberate, declared choice). Duplicate rows for the SAME group x event x class are resolved by delegating to prep_deduplicate_ast (via conflict_action, passed through as its strategy) – not a separate, parallel implementation: identical duplicates always collapse to one first (an n_duplicates_collapsed count is returned, never silently inflating support), and duplicates with DIFFERING R/S/I results are a genuine data conflict, never resolved by taking the first row unless that policy is explicitly chosen – "error" (the default) stops with every conflicting cell named; "drop_conflicts" removes every row for a conflicting cell (never guesses which one is right); "resistant_wins"/ "susceptible_wins"/"first" resolve by the same clinical priority or row-order policy prep_deduplicate_ast already offers elsewhere in the package. Grouping is always by (.group, .event) jointly, so an event_id_col value that repeats ACROSS groups (e.g. a hospital-local patient id reused at a different hospital) is never merged across hospitals – group-scoped identifiers are the default, not an opt-in.

When intermediate_as_resistant is supplied (not NULL), an additional .result_folded column (and its own wide pivot, wide_folded/result_col_folded) is built by delegating to prep_recode_intermediate_ast – the SAME Colistin-aware clinical convention already used elsewhere in anumaan (Colistin I -> S, every other class I -> R), rather than a separate, cruder symmetric I -> R rule. FALSE leaves .result_folded identical to .result (I stays its own category, as before). NULL (the default) skips this step entirely – only the callers that fold at all (profile_audit_support, profile_prepare_model_data) pass a non-NULL value.
